The place

Nine rooms, one long pool, and the forest doing all the talking.

Green beryl is a rare gemstone — quiet, luminous, found only where nature keeps its finest things. That is roughly the whole idea here. A rare find, richly kept.

The rooms face each other across twenty-five metres of water, Minangkabau eaves on both sides in the Negeri Sembilan way, doors that open straight onto the deck.

  • Rooms 9, sleeping 36 in total
  • Pool 25 m · open late
  • From Kuala Lumpur 1 hr 30 min by road
  • Arrive / leave 15:00 · 12:00

The rooms

Nine rooms, three sizes.

They were added a few at a time as the place grew, so they come in three sizes.

In every rate

Same for every room, whichever one you end up in.

  • Parking outside your door
  • Pool until late
  • Fans and air-con
  • Laundry, daily
  • Falls trail guide
  • Coffee, tea, cold water
  • Wi-fi that reaches the deck

A day here

Nothing is scheduled. This is just what tends to happen.

06 : 40

Mist comes off the ridge

It sits in the valley for about an hour.

08 : 15

Breakfast on the veranda

Nasi lemak, fruit from the morning market at Kuala Klawang, eggs however you want them.

11 : 00

The falls trail, 25 minutes on foot

Leaves from the back gate into the Kenaboi reserve, climbs gently, ends at a pool you can stand under.

19 : 30

Lamps on

The strings between the eaves come on at dusk.

23 : 00

Last swim

“Rest is not idleness.” A quiet moment before the day lets go.

Getting here

Ninety minutes from the city, then a smaller road.

From Kuala Lumpur it's about an hour and a half — through Hulu Langat and over the Peras pass, or the easier way down the highway to Seremban and up into Jelebu from there.

The last stretch past Kuala Klawang is a small road and the turn-off is unmarked, so we'll message you a pin the day before.
